payload.title: search results list shows all matches after typing a query
payload.errorMessage:
Timed out 10000ms waiting for expect(locator).toHaveCount(4)

Locator: getByTestId('search-result-row')
Expected: 4
Received: 2

note: The search grid renders half the expected rows (2 of 4, not 0), and a failedRequests entry shows a failed request during the same run — evidence that would normally point toward cascading-env's 'backend is down, so the UI has nothing to render' pattern. But the failing request is a POST to an analytics beacon endpoint (fire-and-forget post-render telemetry, decoupled from the results-fetch endpoint that actually feeds this locator), and the results-fetch call itself is absent from failedRequests — it succeeded. A total backend outage would render zero rows, not a partial set; a partial, non-zero count is the signature of the assertion catching the list mid-repaint. The real cause is a client-side debounce-then-rerender race: the assertion sometimes fires between the search input's debounced re-query and the list's final repaint — not every failedRequests entry is causal, and treating 'a failed request happened somewhere in this run' as sufficient evidence for ENV_ISSUE is exactly the shortcut this case exists to catch.
